seam.mini: Aligned at the back, or painted on the figure's back
seam.deco: Scarf seam, aligned at the back
sup.mini: Tree (organic), 2 interface layers, Z distance 0.1–0.15 mm
sup.edge: Normal, touching the build plate only
sup.eng: Normal; Z distance = 1 layer for a clean underside
sup.flex: Avoid them by orienting the part; if needed, 0.3 mm Z distance
sup.water: Avoid them on walls that must be watertight
sup.dualPla: Interfaces with Support for PLA on the other nozzle
plate.pla: Textured or smooth PEI, no glue
plate.petg: Textured PEI; on smooth PEI, glue stick as a release agent
plate.abs: Textured PEI or Engineering Plate with glue
plate.pc: Engineering Plate or textured PEI with glue stick
plate.tpu: Textured PEI; on smooth PEI, glue as a release agent
dry.pla: 50 °C · 6–8 h (only if it has absorbed moisture)
gt.soak: When the {model} reports the bed at {bed} °C, wait about {m} min before starting: the sensor measures one spot and the rest of the plate takes time to even out.
gt.chActiveHot: Turn on chamber heating to {t} °C and don't start the print until the chamber gets there. Keep the door closed.
gt.chActiveCool: Don't heat the chamber with {mat}. If it goes above ~35 °C, open the door or lid to avoid heat-creep clogs.
gt.chPassiveHot: No chamber heater: preheat with the bed at {bed} °C and the door closed for about {m} min so the air inside reaches 40–45 °C.
gt.chPassiveCool: With {mat}, open the door or remove the top lid: a closed enclosure traps heat and causes heat-creep clogs.
gt.chPetg: With PETG you can print with the door closed, unheated; open it if the chamber goes above 40 °C.
gt.openHot: Open-frame printer: keep it away from windows and air conditioning and, if you can, add an enclosure. Without one, {mat} cracks between layers.
gt.slinger: The bed moves on the Y axis: on tall, narrow parts lower the Y acceleration and add a brim so they don't wobble.
gt.prusaPetg: PETG on smooth PEI: apply glue stick as a release agent or use the textured/satin sheet. PETG bonds so strongly to smooth PEI that it can tear the coating.
gt.loadcell: The load-cell probe touches the plate with the nozzle: plastic left on the tip gives an uneven first layer. Clean it while the nozzle is hot.
pt.x2d.soak: When the X2D reports that the bed has reached {bed} °C, wait about 5 minutes before printing. The firmware heats at full power for 3–5 min to get there fast, but the heat hasn't spread across the whole plate yet: the edges are still colder, and materials like ABS, ASA, PA or PC lift or warp at the corners.
pt.x2d.aux: Print {fil} with the main nozzle: Bambu Lab lists it as “print with caution” on the auxiliary nozzle.
pt.x2d.support: Put support material in the auxiliary nozzle (e.g. Support for PLA on interfaces only): supports come off clean with almost no purge.
pt.x2d.paSupport: For PA or PC supports, use the same material or PVA. “Support for PA/PET” is also listed as “with caution” on the auxiliary nozzle.
pt.x2d.amsDry: The AMS 2 Pro keeps filament dry while printing, but it won't rescue a spool that has already absorbed moisture: dry it first.
pt.x2d.cf: The stock hardened-steel nozzles handle carbon or glass fibre. A 0.6 mm nozzle lowers the risk of clogs.
pt.platePaPc: For PA and PC use the Engineering Plate or textured PEI with a thin layer of glue stick.
pt.tpuExtAms: Load this TPU from the external spool holder, not from the AMS.
pt.tpuRearAms: Load TPU from the rear spool holder, not from the AMS.
pt.h2d.soak: The H2D bed is 350 × 320 mm: when it reports {bed} °C, wait about 6 minutes for the corners to match the centre, especially with ABS, ASA, PA and PC.
pt.h2d.dual: Assign support material to the other nozzle; on large parts you save a lot of time and purge material.
pt.h2d.hotend: Its hotend reaches 350 °C: you can move to the top of the filament's range if layer adhesion is weak.
pt.auxfan: Turn the side auxiliary fan off or down to 30 %: its air stream cracks layers in engineering materials.
pt.cfStockHard: The stock nozzle is hardened steel: fibre-filled filaments are fine.
pt.p1s.cf: The stock nozzle is stainless steel: fibre wears it out within a few spools. Switch to the hardened-steel hotend.
pt.amslite: Don't load TPU into the AMS lite: use the spool holder.
pt.a1.calib: Keep dynamic flow calibration on when changing filament: it compensates for differences between brands.
pt.a1m.bed: The A1 mini bed reaches 80 °C and {fil} needs at least {b} °C: use glue stick and a brim to compensate.
pt.core1.hot: Close the chamber vent so the air inside warms up, and let the printer preheat with the door closed.
pt.core1.cool: Leave the chamber vent open (or the door ajar) so heat doesn't build up.
pt.mk4s.encl: On the open-frame MK4S, an enclosure (Prusa Enclosure or a box) is close to mandatory for this material.
pt.mini.bowden: Bowden extruder: retraction is around 3–3.5 mm. Soft TPU can't be printed reliably.
pt.xl.segbed: The segmented bed only heats the area the part uses: if you add another part after preheating, wait again before printing.
pt.xl.tool: In multi-tool prints, set a standby temperature 30–50 °C lower to avoid oozing.
pt.k2p.soak: The 350 × 350 mm bed of the K2 Plus takes time to even out: when it reads {bed} °C, wait about 8 minutes, longer if the part reaches the corners.
pt.k2p.cfs: Load TPU from the external spool holder, not from the CFS.
pt.e3.hotend: Hotend limited to 260 °C: fine for PLA, PETG and TPU; not suitable for PC or nylon.
pt.e3.speed: The speeds in this sheet are already reduced for its kinematics; going faster makes corners worse (ringing).
pt.n4p.bed: The bed has an inner and an outer zone: if the part extends past the centre, turn on the outer zone and wait for it to even out.
pt.plus4.hotend: The hotend reaches 370 °C: you have headroom at the top of the range if layers don't bond well.
pt.voron.soak: Besides waiting for the bed to reach {bed} °C, the aluminium frame expands as it warms up. With ABS or ASA, heat-soak for 30–60 min with the bed on; otherwise the first layer shifts during the print.
pt.voron.fw: Tune Pressure Advance and Input Shaper in Klipper for every new filament; these values vary a lot between builds.
mt.PLA: PLA softens around 55–60 °C: don't leave it in the sun or inside a car.
Part cooling fan at maximum except on the first layer.
mt.PLA_MATTE: The matte finish hides layer lines, but it's a bit more brittle than regular PLA.
It softens around 55–60 °C: not for parts exposed to heat.
mt.PLA_SILK: Slow outer wall (≤ 60 mm/s) at the top of the temperature range for maximum shine.
Silk PLA bonds layers poorly: don't use it for load-bearing parts.
mt.PLA_CF: It's abrasive: it needs a hardened-steel nozzle.
The matte fibre finish hides layer lines well.
mt.PETG: If it strings: dry it, drop 5 °C and turn on a 0.4 mm Z-hop.
A low fan (20–50 %) improves layer bonding.
mt.PETG_CF: Abrasive: hardened-steel nozzle. It strings less than plain PETG.
Stiffer, with a matte finish; somewhat less tough than unfilled PETG.
mt.ABS: It emits styrene and particles: print with the chamber closed and ventilate the room or use a filter.
mt.ASA: It resists UV: the default choice for outdoor parts.
It gives off fumes like ABS: closed chamber and ventilation.
mt.PC: Without a hot chamber it cracks and lifts: the most demanding material on this list.
Very hygroscopic: always dry it before printing.
mt.PA_CF: It absorbs moisture within minutes: dry it for 8–12 h at 80 °C and print from a dry box (< 20 % RH).
Freshly printed parts are stiffer and more brittle; they gain toughness as they absorb ambient moisture. For maximum stiffness and heat resistance, anneal following the manufacturer's data sheet.
mt.TPU95: Print slowly, with minimal retraction, and keep it out of multi-colour systems.
Dry it: wet TPU bubbles, strings and leaves a rough surface.
mt.TPU85: Soft: it needs a direct-drive extruder with the filament path guided all the way to the gear.
No retraction and low speed; if the filament buckles in the extruder, slow down further.
mt.TPU70: Very soft (70–75A): speed ≤ 20 mm/s and volumetric flow ≤ 1.5 mm³/s.
No retraction. Loosen the extruder tension if it squashes the filament.
Dry it well: it absorbs moisture very quickly.
mt.TPU_HARD: Harder (68D): it does work in Bambu Lab's AMS.
Short retraction (≈ 0.8 mm) and moderate speed.
tt.miniBig: A 0.2 mm (or 0.25 mm) nozzle gains a lot of detail on faces, fingers and weapons.
tt.miniSmall: Fine nozzle: keep the tip clean and the filament dry, every blob shows.
tt.miniDual: Use support material in the second nozzle for interfaces: it peels off without marking the details.
tt.mini: Tilt the figure 30–45° backwards so supports end up on its back.
Minimum layer time of 8–10 s; print several figures at once so each one cools between layers.
tt.car: A car in the sun gets above 70–80 °C inside: ASA, ABS, PC or PA-CF cope; PLA warps.
Orient the part so the load runs along the layers, not pulling them apart.
For clips and mounts, go up to 5–6 walls before raising infill.
tt.deco: Turn on adaptive (variable) layer height: thinner layers on gentle curves and sloped tops.
Matte or silk filament hides lines; glossy dark colours highlight them.
Use a scarf seam in Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer, or paint the seam onto a hidden area.
Ironing only on flat top surfaces.
To remove lines completely: sand (240 → 600 grit) and apply filler primer.
tt.eng: Calibrate flow and Pressure Advance before printing parts with tolerances.
Reference clearances: 0.2 mm for a sliding fit, 0.1 mm for a press fit.
Strength comes mostly from the walls: add walls before adding infill.
Compensate holes: +0.1 mm in XY, or enlarge them in CAD.
tt.draft: Thick layers and lightning infill: you want shape and fit, not strength.
With a 0.6 mm nozzle print time drops by almost half.
tt.flex: 10–20 % gyroid infill gives a soft part; more walls = stiffer.
The filament's Shore hardness rules: 95A feels like a shoe sole, 70–75A like a soft eraser.
tt.outdoor: ASA or PC for outdoors; PLA warps in the sun and PETG fades under UV.
4 or more walls and ≥ 30 % infill so water doesn't get in.
tt.big: If it doesn't fit, split the part and join it with printed pins or dowels.
Brim and, on an enclosed printer, a closed door to avoid warping on long parts.
Adaptive or lightning infill saves material without hurting the surface.
tt.water: More walls (≥ 4) and +3 % flow: water leaks between perimeters, not through the infill.
Vase (spiral) mode if the geometry allows it: one continuous wall with no seam.
An FDM part is not food-safe without a certified coating: the gaps between layers trap bacteria.
a.noTemp: The {model} reaches {max} °C and {fil} needs at least {min} °C. Choose another filament or printer.
a.nzLimited: Nozzle temperature capped at {max} °C, the maximum of the {model}. Print slower to compensate.
a.bed: The bed reaches {max} °C and the manufacturer asks for {b0}–{b1} °C. Use glue stick and a wide brim.
a.cfSoft: {fil} contains fibre and wears out brass or stainless nozzles within hours. Fit a hardened-steel nozzle on the {model}.
a.cfUnk: {fil} is abrasive: check that your nozzle is hardened steel.
a.cfSmall: Fibres clog 0.2–0.25 mm nozzles. Use 0.4 mm or larger (ideally 0.6).
a.open: {mat} on an open printer: high risk of warping and cracks between layers. Use an enclosure, or choose PETG if the part allows it.
a.tpuSoftBowden: Soft TPU ({shore}) doesn't feed reliably through a Bowden extruder.
a.tpuBowden: TPU on a Bowden extruder needs very low speed and almost no retraction.
a.carPla: PLA softens at 55–60 °C and the inside of a car in the sun goes above 70 °C. For this part use ASA, ABS, PC or PA-CF.
a.carPetg: PETG works inside the car in the shade (≈ 70 °C). On the dashboard or parcel shelf, ASA or PC is better.
a.carTpu: TPU works for car gaskets and bumpers, not for structural parts.
a.outPla: PLA doesn't survive the sun: it warps and degrades. ASA or PETG is better.
a.outAbs: ABS yellows and turns brittle under UV. For long outdoor use, choose ASA.
a.flexNo: {fil} isn't flexible. For gaskets or cases choose a TPU (95A, 85A or 75A).
a.miniBig: With a {n} mm nozzle you'll lose a lot of detail. For miniatures use 0.2–0.4 mm.
a.miniCf: Fibre leaves a rough finish that wipes out a miniature's fine details.
a.decoCf: Good choice: the matte fibre finish hides layer lines.
a.water: FDM parts are not safe for food contact without a certified coating.
a.verySoft: Very soft TPU on this machine: print at the speed shown and watch the first layer.
f.support.none: None — same material as the part
f.support.hint: Only materials that work with {mat} are listed.
f.support.noneAvail: No dedicated support material for {mat}: supports use the same material.
r.supUse.interface: Interface only; support body in the main material
r.supUse.full: Full support, or interface only to save material
r.supZ.note: With a different material, the support can touch the part.
rm.limonene: Dissolve in d-limonene, in a ventilated area
sup.withMat: Interfaces in {sup} on the second tool
dry.pva: 55 °C · 8 h; keep it in a dry box
exp.orcaSup: Support filament for OrcaSlicer / Bambu Studio (.json)
a.supTemp: {sup} needs at least {min} °C and the {model} reaches {max} °C.
a.supPvaPetg: {sup} is PVA-based: Bambu Lab warns that printing PETG with a 70 °C bed while using both hotends can clog the PVA nozzle. Keep the bed at 60 °C or lower.
a.supBed: The bed for {mat} ({bed} °C) is well above what {sup} prefers (max {b1} °C): use it for interfaces, not for supports that start on the plate.
a.supX2dPa: On the X2D, both PA-CF and Support for PA/PET are listed “with caution” on the auxiliary nozzle: put the PA-CF in the main nozzle and keep an eye on the support, or use the same material for supports.
st.interfaceOnly: {sup} is for interfaces only: print the support body in the main material to save support filament.
st.cross: PLA and PETG barely bond to each other, which is why one works as an interface for the other. Use 0 mm Z distance and 2–3 interface layers.
st.breakaway: Remove the supports while the part is still warm: with a different-material interface they come off clean.
st.water: Soak the part in warm water (about 40 °C) and change the water when it turns cloudy; stirring speeds it up.
st.limonene: Dissolve HIPS in d-limonene in a closed container for 12–24 h, in a ventilated area.
st.pva: PVA absorbs moisture very quickly: dry it before printing and feed it from a dry box, or it will string and clog.
st.supPa: Remove Support for PA/PET within 2 hours of printing: once it absorbs moisture it sticks. If it does, dry the part.
st.prime: A small prime tower cleans the support nozzle when it returns after standing idle.
mt2.pickSupport: This printer has more than one tool: pick a support material in the form so supports peel off more easily.
mt2.ooze: Turn on ooze prevention and use a small prime tower: idle toolheads ooze a little while they wait.
mt2.standby: Set the standby temperature 30–50 °C below the printing temperature for tools that are used again soon.
mt2.offsets: Recalibrate the tool offsets after changing a nozzle or after a crash; otherwise colours and supports shift.
pt.h2c.left: Only the right nozzle swaps (6 Vortek hotends); the left one is fixed. Put the material you use most, or the support material, on the left.
pt.h2c.heat: Vortek hotends heat by induction in about 8 seconds, so swaps cost little time and support interfaces on every layer are affordable.
pt.u1.cover: Without the optional top cover, stick to PLA, PETG, TPU and PVA. With the cover (and hardened nozzles) it also prints ABS, ASA, PA and PC.
pt.c5.bed: Flashforge notes that with the bed set to 120 °C the actual surface reaches about 100 °C: set a few degrees higher than the filament asks for.
pt.c5p.chamber: Chamber heating is slow: about 10 min to reach 50 °C and about 50 min to reach 65 °C. Start preheating early for PA and PC.
pt.c5.open: The Creator 5 is open-frame: for ABS, ASA, PA and PC the Creator 5 Pro, with its enclosed heated chamber, is the right machine.
sug.lock: I have this printer: don't change it automatically
nz.hint: Ideal nozzle: {n} mm (marked with a dot). Pick the one you have if it's different.
sug.intro: These are the ideal choices for this printer, filament and part. Change them to match the nozzles and support material you have, or the layer height you prefer: the settings update instantly.
sup.hint.ideal: Ideal support: {sup}. Choose another one, or “None”, if you don't have it.
sup.hint.none: This type of part is best printed without supports.
sug.printerBest: Your printer is the best match for this filament and part.
sug.printerOther: For this filament and part, the best-suited printer would be {model}.
sup.cat.filament: Filaments that peel off easily from {mat}
st.tpuPla: PLA is rigid and barely bonds to TPU, so it makes a support that holds the soft part and then separates easily. Print the whole support in PLA, not just the interface. Adhesion varies between brands: if it sticks, leave a 0.1–0.15 mm Z gap.
h.pick: Click to choose a recent query
nz.supHint: Ideal for the support: {n} mm, the same size as the main nozzle, so layer heights line up. The {model} also accepts a different size.
nz.supLocked: The {model} can't mix nozzle sizes in one print: the support nozzle must be the same size as the main one ({n} mm).
nz.supExp: Ideal for the support: {n} mm, the same as the main nozzle. Mixing sizes on the {model} is experimental in PrusaSlicer.
a.supNozMix: The two nozzles are different sizes: use a layer height that works for both (the smaller nozzle sets the limit) and check the {model} slicer profile for each tool.
nz.hint2: Ideal nozzle: {n} mm, {t} (marked with dots). Pick the ones you have if they're different.
nz.supHint2: Ideal for the support: {n} mm, {t}. The same size as the main nozzle keeps layer heights aligned; support materials don't need a hardened or high-flow nozzle.
nz.supLocked2: The {model} needs both nozzles to be the same type and size: the support nozzle must match the main one.
nz.supLockedSize: The {model} can't mix nozzle sizes in one print: the support nozzle must be {n} mm. A {t} nozzle is enough for support materials.
nz.supExp2: Ideal for the support: {n} mm, {t}. Mixing sizes on the {model} is experimental in PrusaSlicer.
a.cfPickHard: {fil} contains fibre and wears out non-hardened nozzles within hours. Choose a hardened nozzle type for the {model}.
a.cfHf: With fibre-filled filaments and high-flow nozzles, Bambu Lab recommends 0.6 mm or larger to avoid clogs.
a.hfTpu: A high-flow nozzle brings no benefit with soft TPU: its speed is limited by the filament, not the hotend.
pt.bigbed.soak: The {model} has a large bed ({w} mm): when it reports {bed} °C, wait about {m} minutes for the corners to match the centre, especially with ABS, ASA, PA and PC.
pt.h3c.temps: Bambu Lab advises against mixing filaments with very different temperature needs in the same job. If you do, set the chamber temperature to 0 in Bambu Studio and remove the AMS 3H side panels.
pt.h3c.swap: Its 9 tools swap in about 6 seconds, so dedicated support material only on the interfaces costs very little time.
pt.k3.open: The K3 is not enclosed: for ABS, ASA, PA or PC use an enclosure or pick a printer with a heated chamber.
pt.k3.swap: KliTek swaps between its 4 nozzles in about 5 seconds: support interfaces in a second material barely add print time.
mt.PA: Unfilled nylon is tough and slightly flexible, but it absorbs moisture fast: dry it 8–12 h at 80 °C and print from a dry box.
It warps a lot: closed chamber, glue stick on the plate and a wide brim.
mt.PA_GF: Glass fibre makes it stiffer and more heat-resistant, and it's abrasive: hardened-steel nozzle, ideally 0.6 mm.
It absorbs moisture within minutes: dry it 8–12 h at 80 °C and print from a dry box.
mt.ABS_GF: The glass fibre reduces warping and shrinkage compared with plain ABS, which makes large flat parts easier.
It emits styrene like ABS: closed chamber and ventilation.
mt.ASA_CF: UV-resistant and stiffer than plain ASA, with a matte finish that hides layer lines.
mt.PC_CF: Stiffer and warps less than plain PC, but it still needs a hot chamber.
Abrasive and hygroscopic: hardened nozzle, and always dry it before printing.
mt.PET_CF: Stiff and dimensionally stable; it absorbs less moisture than nylon, but still dry it 8–12 h at 80 °C.
Abrasive: hardened-steel nozzle. Support for PA/PET works as a breakaway interface.
mt.PPA_CF: High-temperature engineering material: it needs a hotend that reaches 285–320 °C and a hot chamber (≈ 60 °C).
Abrasive and hygroscopic: hardened nozzle, dry it thoroughly and print from a dry box.
mt.PPS_CF: It needs a 310–350 °C hotend: only a few desktop printers can print it.
Very resistant to chemicals and heat; keep the chamber hot (≈ 60 °C) and use a hardened nozzle.
mt.PCTG: Tougher and more impact-resistant than PETG, with similar settings and a bit less stringing.
Like PETG, it bonds very strongly to smooth PEI: use glue stick as a release agent.
dry.pps: Rarely needed (it absorbs little moisture); if in doubt, follow the manufacturer's data sheet
a.gfMild: Bambu Lab doesn't require a hardened nozzle for {fil}, but glass fibre still wears nozzles over time: a hardened one will last much longer.
mt.PLA_TOUGH: Tougher and more impact-resistant than regular PLA, with better layer adhesion: good for functional parts that don't get hot.
It still softens around 60 °C: not for car interiors or parts left in the sun.
mt.PLA_PART: The particles hide layer lines well, but they can clog fine nozzles: use 0.4 mm or larger.
Pick it for looks rather than strength: the particles slightly reduce layer adhesion.
mt.PLA_GLOW: The glow pigment is abrasive: a hardened nozzle is recommended, as it wears brass or stainless nozzles quickly.
Thicker walls and more top layers glow brighter and for longer; charge it under strong or UV light.
mt.PLA_WOOD: Wood fibres can clog small nozzles: use 0.4 mm or larger (0.6 mm is safer) and don't leave the hot nozzle idle for long.
Temperature changes the tone: hotter gives darker wood. It sands and stains well.
mt.PLA_AERO: Foaming filament: hotter means more foam and lighter parts. Start with a flow ratio of ≈ 0.5–0.6 and calibrate at the temperature you'll use.
Avoid long travel moves without extruding and dry it well; it's designed for RC planes and lightweight parts.
mt.ASA_AERO: Foaming ASA: hotter means more foam. Bambu Lab recommends a flow ratio between 0.42 and 0.7 depending on temperature; calibrate on your model.
Like regular ASA it needs an enclosed printer, and it must be very dry.
a.glowSoft: {fil} contains abrasive glow pigment: a hardened nozzle is recommended; a brass or stainless one will wear out.
a.partSmall: The particles in {fil} can clog 0.2–0.25 mm nozzles. Use 0.4 mm or larger.
a.foam: {fil} foams as it prints: the flow ratio shown (≈ 0.6) is only a starting point. Calibrate it at your print temperature; hotter means more foam and less weight.
pt.amsliteNo: Bambu Lab doesn't recommend {fil} in the AMS lite: feed it from the external spool holder.
type.mini.mats: Matte PLA, PLA, PLA+ (sharp detail, easy to paint)
type.car.mats: ASA, ABS-GF, ASA-CF, PC, PA-CF / PA-GF (withstand cabin heat)
type.deco.mats: Matte PLA, silk PLA, PLA Marble / Wood (they hide layer lines)
type.eng.mats: PETG, PCTG, PA-CF / PA-GF, PET-CF, PC; PLA Tough+ for light loads
type.big.mats: PLA, PLA+, PETG; LW-PLA / PLA Aero for lightweight parts
type.water.mats: PETG, PCTG, ASA; PLA for cold liquids only
store.low: Sealed bag or box with desiccant, away from sunlight; it tolerates a few days in room air.
store.mid: Sealed with desiccant (< 20 % RH); after a few days in the open it absorbs moisture and starts stringing or bubbling.
store.high: Very hygroscopic: airtight box with desiccant (< 15–20 % RH) and print straight from a dry box; a few hours in room air can spoil it.
lh.hint: Recommended: {v} mm (marked with a dot). With a {n} mm nozzle, use between {a} and {b} mm.
r.lh.custom: Your choice; the recommended value for this part is {v} mm.
r.lh.rec: Recommended for this nozzle and type of part.
r.lhRange.note: Thinner, extrusion becomes unreliable; thicker, layers bond poorly.
r.lhRange.adaptive: Limits for adaptive layer height: thin layers on curves, thick ones on vertical walls.
ft.trademarks: Brand and product names are trademarks of their owners; this project isn't affiliated with any manufacturer.
